record.original_question: Given a spherical orbifold of volume V, what general upper bound can one place on the size of an isospectral set of spherical orbifolds that contains it?

evidence.quote: Problem 8.2. Let M be a spherical orbifold of volume V. What is an upper bound for the cardinality of an isospectral set of spherical orbifolds which contains M?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M = S^n/\Gamma$ be a spherical orbifold of volume $V$, i.e., the quotient of the round $n$-sphere $S^n$ (of constant sectional curvature $1$) by a finite subgroup $\Gamma$ of $O(n+1)$ acting (possibly with fixed points) by isometries. Two Riemannian orbifolds are said to be isospectral if the Laplace–Beltrami operators on functions have the same eigenvalue spectrum (with multiplicities). An isospectral set of spherical orbifolds containing $M$ is a set $\mathcal{S}$ of mutually isospectral spherical orbifolds (pairwise non-isometric) such that $M \in \mathcal{S}$.

Problem: Find, as a function of $n$ and $V$ only, an explicit upper bound $N(n,V)$ for the cardinality $|\mathcal{S}|$ of any such isospectral set $\mathcal{S}$ of spherical orbifolds containing a spherical orbifold of volume $V$.
artifact.status_search_result: No general upper bound on the cardinality of an isospectral set of spherical orbifolds containing a given orbifold of volume V is known. Recent work (e.g., on isospectral spherical space forms and orbifold lens spaces of highest volume, 2024) studies extremal examples and constructs infinite families of isospectral pairs in some dimensions, but does not provide such a general bound. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Isospectral spherical space forms and orbifolds of highest volume
status_evidence.snippet: The spherical analog of the problem of finding the isospectral hyperbolic orbifolds of smallest volume is to find the isospectral spherical orbifolds of largest volume.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2024) work studies extremal volume problems for isospectral spherical orbifolds but does not establish a general cardinality upper bound in terms of volume.

status_evidence.title: Orbifold Lens Spaces that are Isospectral but not Isometric
status_evidence.snippet: Infinitely many pairs of isospectral non-isometric orbifold lens spaces can be obtained in sufficiently high dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: Large isospectral families of spherical orbifolds exist, so any bound must depend on dimension; no general bound in volume is established.
